definition: Lyra is a lossy audio codec developed by Google that is designed for compressing speech at very low bitrates.
details: Unlike most other audio formats, it compresses data using a machine learning-based algorithm.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. In plain words: Lyra is a lossy audio codec developed by Google that is designed for compressing speech at very low bitrates. Here is how it actually plays out: Unlike most other audio formats, it compresses data using a machine learning-based algorithm. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is Lyra (codec).
